summary: Native Android (no backend, no Expo). Validated the Uber-bubble-mislabels-Bolt-offer regression fix in RideAccessibilityService.collectRoots(). ONE compile-blocking defect FOUND AND FIXED: `android.graphics.Rect` was USED on line 283 (`Rect().also { w.getBoundsInScreen(it) }`) but the import was MISSING — the file as submitted by the main agent did not compile. Added `import android.graphics.Rect` on line 7. After this fix: kotlinc 1.9.22 (JDK 17 aarch64) static compile EXIT 0 on all non-Compose main sources (domain + data + service.accessibility + service.overlay + CsvImporter + CsvExporter) against android-34 jar + stubs. JVM tests: 48/48 PASS (AcceptanceTrackerTest 8, RideParserTest 15, RideParserEdgeCaseTest 8, ProfitabilityEngineTest 10, CsvImporterTest 2, VerdictSoundSynthesizeTest 5). Previous iteration mentioned 43; VerdictSoundSynthesizeTest adds 5 new tests. Logic of collectRoots() reviewed scenario-by-scenario: (a) Bolt foreground + Uber floating bubble → bubble is narrower than 40 % of screen width AND not TYPE_APPLICATION with isActive/isFocused, so it is excluded; Bolt window wins → pkg = com.boltsvc.driver ✓. (b) Bolt offer card over phone home screen (no active VTC window) → bubble filtered by width; Bolt card is wide → sorted first by (active=false), then by area → Bolt wins ✓. (c) Uber alone → Uber TYPE_APPLICATION active window kept → pkg Uber ✓. (d) All VTC windows narrow → fromWindows empty → fallback to rootInActiveWindow if it is a VTC pkg, else returns empty → handleScreen falls back to lastEventPkg (POTENTIAL RESIDUAL RISK, see below). The parser (RideParser.parseHarvest → config.rulesFor(pkg)) consumes exactly this `pkg` string to pick Uber vs Bolt rules, so correct pkg attribution directly fixes the wrong-minutes/wrong-values report. No regression in RideParser, DefaultParserConfig, OfferOverlay.fitFirstRow, isOwnAppInForeground, AcceptanceTracker, CSV import/export — only the pkg-attribution path changed, and parser input (texts) is unchanged.

action_items: FIXED by testing agent (minor): added `import android.graphics.Rect` on line 7 of /app/drivee-copilote/app/src/main/java/com/drivee/copilote/service/accessibility/RideAccessibilityService.kt. The main agent's diff used Rect() on line 283 but omitted the import — static compile failed until this one-line fix was applied. Please verify the import is still present in subsequent iterations (easy to lose in a merge).

CONSIDER (optional, non-blocker): the fallback path in handleScreen uses `lastEventPkg` when collectRoots() returns an empty list. `lastEventPkg` is updated on EVERY onAccessibilityEvent whose pkg is in Platforms.packages, including events fired from the Uber floating bubble. If a user has NO VTC app in foreground (home screen) and the Uber bubble emits an event just before Bolt's offer card is drawn, lastEventPkg could still briefly be Uber while OCR reads Bolt's card. Mitigation idea: in onAccessibilityEvent, only set lastEventPkg when the event's `source` / `windowId` corresponds to a window whose width ≥ 40 %. Or equivalently, in handleScreen's empty-roots branch, re-query `windows` and pick the largest VTC-pkg window regardless of active, falling back to lastEventPkg only when no VTC window exists at all. Low priority: the primary user-reported scenario (Bolt in foreground + Uber bubble floating) is already fully covered by the current fix because fromWindows is non-empty.

CONSIDER (minor hardening): in collectRoots(), the sort currently prefers `active` first then `area`. If TWO VTC windows are both active (split-screen on Android 12+ — rare for driver apps but possible), the one with largest area wins. This is acceptable. If you want deterministic behavior, add a tertiary sort by TYPE_APPLICATION priority (TYPE_APPLICATION > TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY > others).
critical_code_review_comments: 🔴 FOUND & FIXED — missing `import android.graphics.Rect` (used line 283 for `Rect().also { w.getBoundsInScreen(it) }`). File did NOT compile as submitted. One-line fix applied by testing agent (line 7). Everything else in the diff is correct.
✅ `AccessibilityWindowInfo.getBoundsInScreen(Rect)` — verified in android-34 jar, same signature used. API ≥ 21 ✓.

✅ `Triple<AccessibilityNodeInfo, Boolean, Long>` sort: `compareByDescending { it.second }.thenByDescending { it.third }` works because Boolean implements Comparable in Kotlin (true > false → active-first) and Long is Comparable → area-descending. Overflow prevented by `.toLong() * b.height()` on the first multiplicand.

✅ 40 % width threshold: on a 1080-px screen the cutoff is 432 px. A typical Uber bubble is 60–100 px wide (~5–10 %), well below. A Bolt offer card typically fills ≥ 85 % width. Threshold is well-separated from both extremes — safe.
✅ The `root.packageName?.toString() !in Platforms.packages` guard runs BEFORE the width check, so system/launcher windows never leak in; only VTC windows are measured.

✅ The fallback `listOfNotNull(rootInActiveWindow?.takeIf { ... in Platforms.packages })` is unchanged for the pre-regression scenarios (Uber alone, Bolt alone) — only triggered when the `windows` API returns nothing useful, same as before.

✅ The parser consumes the resolved `pkg` directly: `config.rulesFor(pkg)` returns UberRules vs BoltRules → wrong attribution WAS the root cause of wrong minutes/values. The fix targets the exact point where mis-attribution happened.
✅ `isOwnAppInForeground()` (line 261-268) uses the same `windows` + root.packageName check — consistent style with the new collectRoots() code. Both wrapped in runCatching.

✅ No change to RideParser / DefaultParserConfig / OfferOverlay.fitFirstRow / AcceptanceTracker / CsvExporter / CsvImporter was needed or made. Minute and price extraction logic unchanged — the regression was 100 % about which rule-set was applied, not about parsing quality. OfferOverlay.fitFirstRow is a display-only concern. AcceptanceTracker only decides prise/pas prise. CSV is persistence. None of these can distort minutes/price.
ℹ The `windows` API returns top-most windows first on most devices but the ordering IS NOT guaranteed across OEMs. The new sort removes any dependency on list order — a strict improvement.
ℹ `event.text?.forEach` on line 178 raises a Kotlin warning (`unnecessary safe call on a non-null receiver`). Pre-existing — unrelated to this iteration. Low priority cleanup.

rca_of_issue: ROOT CAUSE (confirmed by code reading, matches main agent hypothesis): In the previous collectRoots(), `windows.mapNotNull { it.root }.filter { pkg ∈ Platforms.packages }` relied on the OS-provided window order where the top-most window is first. When the driver is signed in on BOTH Uber and Bolt and currently has Bolt in the foreground, the Uber driver app keeps its always-on-top floating 'go online' bubble visible — that bubble is a TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY whose root packageName is com.ubercab.driver and which sits TOPMOST. firstOrNull() therefore returned the Uber bubble's root → pkg = Uber → config.rulesFor("com.ubercab.driver") returned UberRules → the Bolt offer card (read via accessibility nodes merged across sameApp roots, or via OCR of the full screen) was parsed with Uber keyword rules (approach/ride/pickup/EN) instead of Bolt rules (prise en charge/trajet/FR). Numeric values that happen to match Uber's price-with-asterisk / minutes-pattern were extracted from Bolt's text in the wrong semantic slots → the pop-up showed 'UBER' + wrong minutes + wrong values. FIX APPLIED by main agent (and validated here): collectRoots() now (1) requires window width ≥ 40 % of screen width — this filters out all small floating-bubble overlays whatever their package; (2) sorts remaining VTC windows by (active+focused TYPE_APPLICATION first, then largest area) — this guarantees the foreground VTC app wins over any still-wide secondary overlay. One-line COMPILE FIX from testing agent: added missing `import android.graphics.Rect` so the Rect() constructor on line 283 resolves. VERIFICATION: 48/48 JVM tests still pass, kotlinc EXIT 0, scenario walk-through (a-d) all produce the expected pkg. REPRODUCTION STEPS on device (for main agent self-test): sign in on both Uber Driver and Bolt Driver; put Bolt in foreground; wait for Uber bubble to appear; trigger a Bolt offer card. Before the fix the overlay displays 'UBER' header with Uber-parsed values; after the fix it displays 'BOLT' with correct minutes/price. MITIGATION-ALREADY-IN-CODE: self-read guard from iter 10 still blocks OCR when VTC Copilot is foreground; AcceptanceTracker unchanged. RESIDUAL RISK (optional follow-up, see action_items): if ever collectRoots() returns empty, handleScreen falls back to lastEventPkg which is still updated by Uber-bubble events — a narrow edge case the main agent may want to harden by filtering events from small windows at the onAccessibilityEvent entry point.
